question: One day after undergoing surgery for a traumatic right pelvic fracture, a 73-year-old man has pain over his buttocks and scrotum and urinary incontinence. Physical examination shows right-sided perineal hypesthesia and absence of anal sphincter contraction when the skin around the anus is touched. This patient is most likely to have which of the following additional neurological deficits?

The presence of urinary incontinence, right-sided perineal hypesthesia, and absence of anal sphincter contraction suggests damage to the nerves responsible for these functions. The most relevant additional neurological deficit is likely 'Absent reflex erection' (option opb), as this is associated with sacral nerve involvement. The chains indicating 'Impaired psychogenic erection' (option opc) and 'Absent cremasteric reflex' (option ope) are also plausible but less directly linked to the acute presentation. 'Paralysis of hip adductors' (option opa) and 'Impaired hip flexion' (option opc) are less likely as they do not directly correlate with the described symptoms of perineal nerve damage. Therefore, the best-supported option is 'Absent reflex erection' due to the involvement of the sacral nerves.
